Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.    I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

Rock Hill, SC • (704) 999-3605 • Matthewstydsw27@gmail.com

October 27, 2026
Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Mooresville, NC

Re: Clinic Director: Adolescent Mental Health | Launch AWA North Carolina

Dear Hiring Committee:
I am excited to apply for the Clinic Director position leading the launch of Adolescent Wellness Academy’s first North Carolina clinic. As a licensed clinical social work and case management leader with more than 15 years of experience across behavioral health, healthcare, higher education, and community services, I offer the clinical supervision, operational leadership, and change-management experience needed to build a strong program from the ground up. AWA’s opportunity to create a focused, family-centered PHP/IOP clinic for adolescents is especially compelling to me because it combines direct clinical impact with the chance to shape culture, quality, and sustainable growth from day one.

Throughout my career, I have led complex case coordination, crisis response, care transitions, quality assurance, policy development, talent development, budgeting, and resource allocation. I have also provided clinical supervision and operational management while partnering with healthcare providers, hospital leaders, community agencies, and other stakeholders. These experiences would enable me to recruit and develop clinicians, establish clear clinical and documentation standards, guide level-of-care decisions, and build trusted relationships with families and referral partners across North Carolina.

I would bring a practical, outcomes-focused approach to launch execution: hiring and onboarding a cohesive team; creating a supportive environment for early-career clinicians; establishing reliable crisis, documentation, and quality-review processes; and using assessment findings and utilization trends to strengthen care delivery. My Master of Social Work and ongoing Doctor of Social Work studies in leadership further support my ability to connect evidence-informed clinical practice with disciplined operations and organizational growth.

AWA’s values—Dare to Grow, Contribute to the Whole, Choose Kindness, Spread Optimism, and Deliver Results—reflect how I strive to lead: with accountability, collaboration, compassion, and a clear commitment to excellent outcomes. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical and operational leadership can help AWA launch a high-quality adolescent program and establish a strong foundation for long-term success in North Carolina.
Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Ty Matthews, LCSW, LISW-CP, DSW (C)

Celena Ditz, MS, LMFT
Kings Mountain, NC
(704) 418-2440 | celditz@gmail.com

October 26, 2026

Hiring Committee
Launch AWA NC
Re: Clinic Director – Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Clinic Director – Adolescent Mental Health position with Launch AWA NC. As a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist with more than 25 years of experience in clinical and child-and-family services, including over 15 years in program and clinical leadership, I bring a combination of clinical expertise, operational management, staff development, and a strong commitment to improving outcomes for children, adolescents, and families. I am excited about the opportunity to apply my experience to a role focused on adolescent mental health and the delivery of high-quality, accessible clinical services.

In my current role as Director of Programs at Children’s Homes of Cleveland County/Core Family Services, I provide senior clinical and operational leadership across outpatient therapy, residential, independent living, and adoption programs. I also serve as Clinical Director of outpatient therapy, where I oversee clinical quality, clinician recruitment and supervision, service capacity, reimbursement, compliance, and ongoing program development. Throughout my tenure, I have worked to strengthen clinical services, support staff effectiveness, and ensure that programs meet the needs of the individuals and families they serve while maintaining appropriate clinical, contractual, and regulatory standards.

My experience has provided me with a strong understanding of the balance required to lead a successful behavioral health clinic. I have experience developing clinical capacity in response to community needs, supporting clinicians through supervision and consultation, managing after-hours clinical coverage for therapeutic emergencies, and collaborating with executive leadership on staffing, budgeting, and organizational planning. I believe effective clinical leadership requires both a commitment to sound clinical practice and the ability to build the systems, relationships, and processes that allow clinicians to provide meaningful, consistent care.

I also bring extensive experience in trauma-informed care, quality improvement, and clinical standards. As a Statewide Clinical Coach with Benchmarks NC Partnering for Excellence, I train, review, and evaluate trauma-intensive clinical assessments completed by clinicians across North Carolina, providing feedback and supporting consistency with established clinical standards. Additionally, I coordinate my agency’s performance and quality improvement and accreditation activities, including staff training, record reviews, corrective action planning, and continuous improvement initiatives. These experiences have strengthened my ability to evaluate clinical practices, identify opportunities for improvement, support professional development, and promote accountability while maintaining a focus on quality care.

In addition to my clinical background, I hold a Master of Science in Marriage and Family Therapy and a Master of Business Administration. This combination allows me to approach clinical leadership with an understanding of both the therapeutic needs of adolescents and families and the operational and financial considerations necessary to sustain and grow effective services. I value collaborative leadership, clear communication, thoughtful decision-making, and creating an environment where clinicians feel supported in their work and equipped to provide the highest quality of care.

Throughout my career, I have remained committed to serving children and families, particularly those impacted by trauma and other significant life challenges. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my experience to Launch AWA NC and help strengthen mental health services for adolescents. Given my extensive experience, clinical background, and leadership responsibilities, I would also welcome a conversation about compensation. I recognize that the position has a posted salary range; however, I am seeking compensation above that range that more fully reflects my qualifications and the value I would bring to the role. I hope there may be flexibility to discuss a package that aligns with my experience and the position’s responsibilities.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, leadership experience, and commitment to serving adolescents and families could contribute to the continued success of Launch AWA NC.

Sincerely,
Celena Ditz, MS, LMFT

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,


I am excited to express my interest in the position of Program Operations Manager in Adolescent Behavioral Health. With over 15 years of experience in project management and recruitment in the international education industry, managing both employees and independent contractors, I am confident that I would be a great fit for this position.

My career in management started in Japan where I oversaw schools with a large and diverse staff. This experience introduced me to people and project management, and allowed me to grow my skills in a fast-paced environment.

After returning to the United States, I joined EF Education First and had the opportunity to work with both recruitment and operations for a variety of global centers. I gained knowledge essential to workflows and processes, and local and international hiring regulations. When I was promoted to Procurement and Support manager, I excelled in data management and had the chance to collaborate with operations managers to improve the quality of teachers in the center.

Currently the focus of my role is recruitment and support for independent contractors. I lead and collaborate to analyze the KPIs and thought leadership strategy for our centers. I’ve had the chance to work with people from all across the globe and truly value the opportunity to work in a diverse and engaging environment.

I look forward to having the chance to join Adolescent Wellness Academy, and discussing my qualifications in further detail.

Thank you for your consideration.


All the best,

Stefany Gamba

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I’m excited to apply for the remote Utilization Review Specialist – Behavioral Health position at Principles Recovery Center. My background combines hands-on behavioral health documentation and review support with outpatient addiction and mental health program leadership, giving me a strong foundation for the role’s authorization and medical-necessity workflows.

In my current role as Behavioral Health Documentation & Review Support at Kings Consulting and Analytics, LLC, I support documentation review for substance use disorder and mental health cases. I review intakes, diagnoses, treatment history, progress notes, service documentation, and supporting clinical records to identify gaps and help ensure records are complete, consistent, and ready for utilization review. I also synthesize clinical details in EHR/KIPU workflows to support authorization-related documentation, level-of-care alignment, and timely review decisions. Working alongside an experienced behavioral health consulting team has strengthened my review accuracy and understanding of utilization review processes.

Previously, as Program Director at Meta Addiction Treatment, I developed substantial experience in outpatient addiction and mental health services, program leadership, and case management. That work strengthened my ability to coordinate across teams, support treatment planning and continuity of care, maintain clear documentation, and keep client needs and program requirements in view.

I’m prepared to bring this experience to benefit and eligibility verification, prior authorization and pre-certification workflows, concurrent and continued-stay reviews, and medical-necessity support. My background includes supporting level-of-care alignment and authorization documentation; I’m ready to build on that foundation with the specific review standards and procedures used by Principles Recovery Center.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my documentation review experience and behavioral health program background can contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Lindsey Duran

October 28, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in youth development, art instruction, creative education, and community programming, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to an environment dedicated to supporting adolescents’ well-being, personal development, and growth.

My experience working with children and teens through the Boys & Girls Club and the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp has strengthened my appreciation for the importance of creating positive, structured, and encouraging environments where young people can develop confidence, explore their strengths, and express themselves constructively. Through art instruction and guided creative workshops, I have facilitated activities that incorporate painting, storytelling, imagination, and self-expression to encourage creativity, personal growth, and meaningful engagement.

In 2025, I served as an art instructor for the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp, delivering structured art workshops for children and teenagers. I also led a community painting experience at JPP International Church through Painting With A Twist, facilitating an engaging group activity for approximately 40 participants. Earlier in my career, my work with the Boys & Girls Club involved youth art programming designed to encourage imagination, confidence, and self-expression. These experiences have reinforced my belief that young people benefit from opportunities to discover their abilities, develop positive relationships, and engage in activities that promote healthy self-expression.

I currently serve as Program Coordinator for Paint With Purpose, a community arts and creative wellness initiative that uses guided painting experiences to encourage self-expression, confidence, healing, and connection. My responsibilities include developing and coordinating creative workshops, planning activities, preparing materials, communicating with participants, and exploring partnerships with community organizations and schools. This work reflects my commitment to using creativity as a constructive way to bring people together and create meaningful community experiences.

In addition to my experience in youth programming and the arts, I bring more than 10 years of experience in administrative support, client relations, organizational coordination, and professional communication. My background includes supporting leadership, coordinating schedules and activities, managing documentation, and handling confidential information with discretion. These skills would allow me to contribute organization, reliability, professionalism, and effective communication to your team.

I am also pursuing a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology at South Florida Bible College, with anticipated completion in 2028. My educational path complements my interest in human development, individual strengths, and the factors that contribute to personal growth and well-being. As an artist, published children’s book author, and creative educator, I am passionate about helping people recognize their potential and discover constructive ways to communicate and express themselves. My CPR and AED certification, obtained in 2023, further reflects my commitment to maintaining relevant practical skills.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, creativity, compassion, and organizational strengths to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to a supportive environment where adolescents are encouraged to develop healthy coping strategies, build confidence, strengthen interpersonal skills, and recognize their capacity for growth. I would be proud to contribute to a team that approaches youth development with professionalism, respect, consistency, and an understanding of the importance of individualized support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in youth development, creative programming, psychology studies, and professional administration could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and its mission.

Sincerely,

Shamaiah Manriquez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I am especially drawn to AWA Academy because of the impact your work has on the lives of children and families, and I would love to be part of that mission.

I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. I also have experience working in an inpatient psychiatric hospital with adults, where I facilitated group therapy and conducted intake assessments. These experiences have helped me build my clinical skills, connect with clients from different backgrounds, and better understand the importance of compassionate, individualized care.

Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. Working with children and families was one of the most meaningful parts of my professional journey and played a big role in shaping the kind of therapist I wanted to become. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. I would love the opportunity to bring that passion into my clinical work with adolescents and their families.

My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I am eager to learn, grow, and challenge myself as a clinician, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to do so alongside a team that shares my commitment to supporting young people through difficult moments in their lives.

I am also fluent in both English and Portuguese, which allows me to connect with and support families from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. I currently hold a license as a Registered Mental Health Intern and have a qualified supervisor. I anticipate to become fully licensed in a year and a half.

I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Thank you!

Rebecca Ubertini

October 23, 2026 

Dear Hiring Committee, 

Thank you for taking the time to review my resume and cover letter. I am writing to express my enthusiasm for the opportunity to continue my experience working as a Registered Mental Health Counseling Intern at  Adolescent Wellness Academy. I received a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and am a recent graduate with my Masters in Mental Health Counseling from the University of Miami. 

As a motivated and compassionate clinician, I am interested in expanding my experience of working with evidence-based treatment modalities. 

My educational experiences have helped me to build my knowledge and experience for working as a registered mental health counseling intern. I have a strong academic background in psychology, as well as a strong interest in working with children and their families to address mental health challenges at an early age, including Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Anxiety, and Depression. Through my recent experiences working as a practicum intern at Nicklaus Children’s Hospital and the Institute for Individual and Family Counseling, I was able to establish a strong foundation in conceptualizing cases, applying interventions and building rapport. 

In my previous experience working at Florida International University’s Summer Treatment Program, I had the opportunity to work directly with children and their families, providing support in areas such as emotional regulation, coping skills, and behavioral management. These experiences have provided a good foundation in implementing therapeutic strategies tailored to the unique needs of young children, as well as solidified my interest in child and adolescent mental health. 

I have a passion for working with programs that help to provide low-cost services for a diverse population, as highlighted in my experience working as a practicum intern at the institute for Individual and Family Counseling. I believe that my strong communication skills and dedication will allow for a wonderful learning experience as I continue my work in the field of mental health counseling.  

I have included my resume and look forward to the possibility of discussing further my qualifications. Please feel welcome to contact me at your earliest convenience. I look forward to hearing from you. 

Respectfully, 
Morgan Reilly

Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Boca Raton, Florida


Re: Primary Therapist Position

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) in Boca Raton, Florida. With a Ph.D. in Counselor Education and Supervision, a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and experience in clinical practice, counselor education, and clinical training, I bring an integrated perspective on mental health care that combines evidence-informed clinical approaches, developmental knowledge, multicultural awareness, and a commitment to supporting individuals through challenging life transitions. Having recently relocated back to Florida from Connecticut, I am currently working toward full licensure with the State of Florida and practicing as a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI). I am also legally authorized to live and work in the United States without employer sponsorship. I am particularly interested in AWA’s work with adolescents and its emphasis on individualized, collaborative care that supports emotional well-being, resilience, and personal growth, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to AWA’s work with adolescents and families from diverse backgrounds.

As a Portuguese-English bilingual professional with Spanish skills, I bring a multicultural perspective that supports my commitment to culturally responsive and accessible mental health care. My Brazilian background and international experience have shaped my appreciation for the ways culture, identity, family expectations, and transitions influence individuals’ experiences and help-seeking behaviors. I recognize the importance of building therapeutic relationships that honor clients’ culture and lived experiences while fostering trust, collaboration, and respect. 

My clinical experience and interests include working with concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma, substance use/abuse, domestic violence, acculturation, relationship difficulties, and life transitions. My therapeutic approach reflects evidence-informed assimilative integration, grounded primarily in Narrative Therapy and Relational-Cultural Theory (RCT), while incorporating complementary approaches such as Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to meet clients’ unique needs and therapeutic goals. I strive to create a warm, collaborative, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment in which clients can explore their experiences, identify strengths, develop effective coping strategies, and work toward meaningful goals. My approach is grounded in cultural humility, trauma-responsive care, and an understanding of how relationships, family systems, cultural contexts, and broader social factors influence mental health and development.

I have a particular interest in human development across the lifespan, which is reflected in both my clinical work and my teaching. As an instructor, I have taught Lifespan and Human Development to counseling students, a course that deepens my engagement with developmental theories and how biological, psychological, social, cultural, and relational factors shape individuals’ experiences and well-being at different stages of life. This academic focus complements my interest in working with adolescents and understanding the unique developmental, emotional, interpersonal, and family-related challenges they may experience. I value developmentally responsive, trauma-informed, and strengths-based approaches that recognize each young person’s needs while engaging families and other members of the treatment team to support growth, resilience, and emotional well-being.

My clinical background also includes experience with individuals with autism and intellectual disabilities. In Brazil, I developed a project focused on social inclusion and group counseling for individuals with developmental disabilities, which gave me valuable experience understanding and addressing social, interpersonal, developmental, and emotional needs. This experience strengthened my commitment to adapting support to individuals’ unique circumstances and fostering environments that promote inclusion, connection, and personal growth. My background in career counseling further strengthened my experience supporting young individuals as they navigate transitions, develop self-awareness, and identify meaningful paths forward.

In addition to my clinical work, I served as an Assistant Professor of Practice and Clinical Training Director at Fairfield University in Connecticut, where I taught and mentored counseling students, coordinated clinical placements, collaborated with clinical supervisors and community partners, and supported students’ professional development. My responsibilities included coordinating field placements, communicating with supervisors and training sites, and helping students connect academic knowledge with clinical practice. This experience strengthened my ability to respectfully collaborate across professional roles, communicate effectively, maintain organized documentation, and appreciate the importance of coordinated care and professional accountability. My teaching experience in counseling skills, advanced treatment and counseling interventions, group work, ethics, career counseling, and human development also informs my understanding of therapeutic relationships, treatment planning, and the importance of adapting interventions to clients’ developmental and contextual needs.

I believe I am drawn to AWA’s multidisciplinary treatment environment and the opportunity to collaborate with therapists, psychiatrists, and other clinical professionals to support adolescents’ mental health and well-being. I value comprehensive, individualized treatment that integrates assessment, collaborative goal setting, therapeutic interventions, ongoing progress evaluation, family engagement, and continuity of care. I also recognize the importance of timely, accurate clinical documentation, ethical practice, appropriate consultation, and coordination with the treatment team to promote effective, consistent care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, expertise in counselor education and human development, multicultural perspective, and commitment to accessible, trauma-responsive, strengths-based, and evidence-informed care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and the adolescents and families it serves.

Sincerely,

Paula Lazarim, Ph.D., M.S., NCC
Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a bachelor’s degree in Psychology, a Master of Business Administration, and a diverse professional background in social services, case management, customer service, and client support, I believe I possess the interpersonal, organizational, and administrative skills necessary to make a meaningful contribution to your admissions team.

Throughout my professional career, I have developed a strong passion for helping individuals and families navigate challenging circumstances while ensuring they feel heard, supported, and respected. My experience in child protective services and social services has provided me with valuable skills in assessing individual needs, conducting sensitive conversations, gathering critical information, maintaining accurate documentation, and coordinating services and resources. I understand the importance of approaching every interaction with empathy, professionalism, confidentiality, and an understanding that individuals may be reaching out during some of the most difficult moments in their lives.

In addition to my direct service experience, my background in customer service and administrative support has strengthened my ability to manage multiple responsibilities, communicate effectively, maintain detailed records, and provide consistent follow-up. I am comfortable working independently, adapting to changing priorities, and utilizing technology to maintain organization and accountability in a fast-paced environment. I also recognize the importance of confidentiality, accuracy, and compliance when handling sensitive client information.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to serve as an initial point of contact for individuals and families seeking behavioral health and substance use treatment. I strongly believe that the first interaction can make a lasting impression, and I would welcome the opportunity to help prospective clients feel comfortable taking the next step toward receiving the care and support they need.

I would be honored to bring my educational background, professional experience, compassion, and commitment to quality service to your growing team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and dedication to helping others align with the needs of your organization.

Sincerely,

Brianne Durham

Dear Hiring Manager, 
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I graduated from Northern Michigan University in May 2026 with a Bachelor of Science in Psychology, concentrating in Mental Health/Pre-Clinical, and hold a Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) certification. With my education and hands-on experience in behavioral healthcare, I would love the opportunity to build upon my skills in client support, communication, and behavioral health as a part of your admissions team. 
Through my experience as an ABA Aid and Registered Behavior Technician with Copper Country Mental Health, I have developed a strong understanding of the importance of compassionate, individualized care when working with people of diverse behavioral, developmental, and emotional needs. I have experience establishing rapport with clients and families, maintaining professional boundaries, documenting client progress, and supporting individualized treatment plans. My academic background in psychology has further prepared me for this role. A few of my classes included Abnormal Psychology, Substance Use Disorder Social Work, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Health Psychology, and Human Behavior Psychology. These classes have given me a valuable foundation in mental health, substance use disorders, and the challenges individuals and families may face when seeking treatment as well as how to support them. 
I also have experience with HIPAA awareness, patient confidentiality, and maintaining accurate behavioral health documentation, as I was given trainings in these during my ABA aid Training with Copper Country Mental Health. Additionally, my experience owning and operating Senia Faye Photography has allowed me to independently manage client inquiries, coordinate scheduling, maintain consistent follow-up, and guide prospective clients from their initial contact through completed bookings. Managing my own business has taught me to take initiative, stay organized, manage multiple tasks, and provide a positive client experience. 
I believe these experiences and skills have prepared me for managing admissions inquiries and helping people and families navigate the intake process. What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to be a supportive first point of contact for clients and families seeking mental health services. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be an overwhelming and vulnerable experience, and I would approach every interaction with patience, empathy, professionalism, and respect. I would welcome the opportunity to help make that first step toward treatment feel more approachable and reassuring. 
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my education, behavioral healthcare experience, and communication skills could contribute to your admissions team. I look forward to hearing from you.

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am excited to apply for this position with your organization. While my professional background has primarily been in retail leadership, the experiences that have shaped me over the past several years have confirmed that my true passion is helping children reach their fullest potential.
After serving as an Assistant Store Manager with both Aldi and Walgreens, I stepped away from traditional employment following my daughter's autism diagnosis. Since then, I have dedicated myself to learning everything I can about autism, supporting her daily development, collaborating with her therapy team, and creating structured routines that encourage growth and independence. Watching the positive impact of evidence-based intervention has inspired me to pursue a Bachelor of Science in Psychology with a concentration in Applied Behavior Analysis, where I currently maintain a 4.0 GPA.
In addition to my education, I have continued developing professionally by operating my own small business, which has strengthened my organizational skills, communication, accountability, and ability to manage competing priorities. My previous leadership roles also taught me how to coach others, remain calm under pressure, solve problems efficiently, and build trusting relationships with people from many different backgrounds.
Although I am beginning my professional career in ABA, I bring something that cannot be taught in a classroom alone: the perspective of a parent who understands both the challenges and the hope that families experience. I know how meaningful compassionate, patient, and consistent support can be, and I would be honored to provide that same level of care to the children and families your organization serves.
I am eager to continue learning under experienced professionals while contributing my work ethic, empathy, and commitment to delivering high-quality behavioral services. Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background, education, and personal experiences have prepared me to become a valuable member of your team.
Sincerely,
Kristian Wright

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. My background includes crisis response, intake assessments, case management, and helping people connect with appropriate services.

Originally from Canada, I have lived in Washington for the past three years. Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. With a Bachelor's degree in Applied Behavior Science, professional experience providing behavioral services to children and adolescents, and a background in the United States Air Force, I bring a combination of behavioral health knowledge, communication skills, and professional accountability that I believe would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role as a Registered Behavior Technician, I provide remote ABA services to children and teenagers, supporting their development of essential life skills, social skills, and personal independence. Alongside direct client services, I maintain daily communication with parents and guardians through virtual interactions and email correspondence. This has allowed me to develop strong communication skills, build professional relationships with families, address questions, and understand the importance of providing consistent and supportive communication throughout a client's care.

My previous experience in clinic-based ABA services has also given me the opportunity to work with younger children and support individualized developmental goals. Combined with my academic background in Applied Behavior Science, these experiences have provided me with a strong foundation in behavioral health and a greater understanding of the needs of children, adolescents, and their families.

Before entering the behavioral health field, I served in the United States Air Force as a Security Forces member. This experience strengthened my attention to detail, ability to follow established protocols, organizational skills, and ability to remain professional and composed while handling important responsibilities.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to apply my behavioral health experience and communication skills in a role that helps adolescents and their families access the support they need. As someone already experienced in remote service delivery, I am comfortable managing responsibilities independently, maintaining consistent communication, and staying organized in a virtual environment. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my education, experience, and dedication to your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and qualifications could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,

Devan Garcia

Supporting individuals through mental health challenges and substance use recovery has become one of the most meaningful aspects of my professional journey. I have developed a strong passion for helping young people feel understood, supported, and empowered to make positive changes in their lives. With hands-on experience in substance use treatment, behavioral interventions, and individualized client care, I am eager to bring my skills and dedication to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

During my time as a CPST Provider at The Counseling Center, Inc., I worked directly with individuals experiencing substance use disorders and co-occurring mental health conditions. My responsibilities included conducting level-of-care assessments, assisting with individualized treatment planning, providing case management, and facilitating individual and group interventions. I gained experience in motivational interviewing, relapse prevention, psychoeducation, and helping clients develop healthy coping strategies. This position strengthened my ability to build trusting relationships, approach sensitive situations without judgment, and support individuals through challenging stages of recovery.

In my current position as a Registered Behavior Technician at Apollo Behavior, I work one-on-one with children who have autism spectrum disorder and developmental delays. I implement individualized behavioral treatment plans, teach communication and daily living skills, assist with managing challenging behaviors, and collaborate with clinical supervisors and families. This experience has strengthened my patience, adaptability, crisis prevention skills, and ability to provide compassionate, person-centered care.

I am also pursuing an undergraduate degree in Clinical Psychology at Ohio University and hold a CDCA Preliminary credential, my RBT license in the state of Georgia, along with CPR and First Aid certifications. My education and professional experiences have reinforced my commitment to the behavioral health field, particularly supporting young people who face mental health challenges, substance use concerns, and difficult life circumstances.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to make a meaningful difference during such an important stage of a young person’s life. I understand the importance of creating a safe, supportive, and judgment-free environment where adolescents feel heard, respected, and encouraged to make positive changes. I would be proud to contribute my experience, dedication, and genuine passion for mental health and recovery services to your organization.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills align with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of joining your team and helping adolescents build healthier, more successful futures.

I am excited to express my interest in the Adolescent Mental Health Admission Coordinator position. With over 17 years of experience in the corrections field, including extensive experience working with juvenile populations, as well as a professional background in mental health services, I believe I bring a valuable combination of experience, knowledge, and compassion to this position.

One of the most valuable parts of my professional background was serving as an Inpatient Coordinator at Middle Tennessee Mental Health Institute (MTMHI). My 17 years in corrections have also allowed me to develop strong communication, crisis management, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills. Working with juveniles and individuals experiencing behavioral and mental health challenges has taught me the importance of patience, empathy, consistency, and understanding. I recognize that adolescents facing mental health struggles need more than a placement or admission; they need people who genuinely care about their well-being and understand the importance of getting them the help they deserve.

Mental health is a field that is very near and dear to my heart. I am passionate about making a difference in the lives of individuals and families navigating mental health challenges. candidates.cover_letter:
Jacob Kingsley
Hillsdale, Michigan

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over six years of experience in behavioral health at Hillsdale Hospital, I have developed a strong understanding of mental health challenges, patient needs, and the importance of connecting individuals and families with appropriate care and support.

In my current role as a Psychiatric Technician, I work directly with individuals experiencing a wide range of mental health challenges and crises. My responsibilities include patient observation, safety monitoring, de-escalation, documentation, and building therapeutic relationships. Throughout my experience, I have learned that meaningful support often begins with something simple: listening without judgment, showing compassion, and helping someone feel comfortable enough to accept help.

What particularly interests me about Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to help adolescents and their families navigate the process of seeking mental health treatment. I understand that reaching out for help can be an intimidating and emotional experience, especially for parents who are concerned about their child's well-being. I believe every family deserves to be met with patience, understanding, and reassurance. I would take pride in being a welcoming and supportive first point of contact during such an important time.

My background has strengthened my ability to communicate effectively, remain calm under pressure, handle sensitive situations, and work collaboratively with patients, families, and healthcare professionals. I also bring experience with clinical documentation, maintaining patient confidentiality, and recognizing when concerns need to be escalated. In addition, I hold CPR/BLS certification, TEAM and CPI training, and have served as a TEAM instructor.

While my experience has primarily been in direct patient care, I am eager to apply those skills in an admissions and coordination capacity. I am confident in my ability to learn new systems and processes while bringing the compassion, professionalism, organization, and follow-through that this position requires.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my behavioral health experience, dedication to patient care, and genuine desire to help others could make me a valuable addition to the Adolescent Wellness Academy team.

Sincerely,
Jacob Kingsley

In my previous role as an RTC Liaison/Case Manager with MHMR, I worked closely with individuals, families, treatment providers, schools, probation officers, and community agencies to coordinate behavioral health services and residential treatment placements. My responsibilities included completing assessments, facilitating referrals, developing and coordinating individualized treatment plans, supporting crisis prevention efforts, monitoring placement processes, and maintaining consistent communication with families and multidisciplinary teams. I also bring experience managing detailed case documentation, maintaining electronic medical records, tracking treatment progress, coordinating appointments and transitions, and handling confidential information with professionalism and discretion. My background has required strong organization, attention to detail, timely follow-up, and the ability to manage multiple cases and competing priorities while ensuring individuals and families receive consistent communication and support. These skills translate directly to admissions coordination, referral management, intake preparation, and maintaining accurate CRM and EMR records.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to be a reassuring first point of contact for individuals and families navigating mental health or substance use treatment. I understand that reaching out for help can be overwhelming, especially for parents seeking care for their teenagers or individuals experiencing challenges with substance use and co-occurring mental health conditions. I believe effective admissions coordination requires more than answering calls; it requires active listening, empathy, clear communication, follow-through, and the ability to make people feel heard and supported while guiding them toward the appropriate next step.

My educational background in psychology and human services, combined with my professional experience supporting vulnerable populations, has prepared me to approach each interaction with compassion, professionalism, and respect. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my behavioral health knowledge, communication skills, and commitment to continuity of care to your admissions team.
